name: Milan
tagline: Italy's capital of fashion, design and quiet wealth.
bestMonths: Mar, Apr, May, Jun, Oct and Nov
whenBlurb: Spring and early autumn are ideal, framed by the Fashion Weeks and April's Design Week; August empties out and much closes, and winters run foggy.

ourTake.lede: Milan is a working luxury city, not an open-air museum, its pleasures are the shops, the aperitivo hour and one or two great sights done properly. Book Leonardo's Last Supper weeks ahead; it is the one thing you cannot walk up to. Skip the crowded Duomo rooftop queue at midday and go at opening, then spend the evening in the Brera lanes.
ourTake.comeIf: You want fashion, design and aperitivo, and Lake Como an hour up the road.
ourTake.skipIf: You want ruins and postcard Italy over style and shopping.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Bvlgari Hotel Milano
items.description: The jeweller's Milanese house, a hidden 18th-century palazzo with a vast private garden, a cul-de-sac from Via Montenapoleone.

items.name: Four Seasons Hotel Milano
items.description: A serene former Renaissance convent in the heart of the fashion quarter, cloistered gardens and the surest hands in Milan.

items.name: Mandarin Oriental, Milan
items.description: Four linked 18th-century palazzi on a discreet backstreet beside La Scala, the city's only Forbes Five-Star.

items.name: Portrait Milano
items.description: A Ferragamo-family house built around Milan's oldest Baroque seminary courtyard, the address of the moment.

items.name: Armani Hotel Milano
items.description: Mr Armani's own vision of stay, greige calm and 'stay with Armani' service on Via Manzoni.

items.name: Hotel Principe di Savoia, Dorchester Collection
items.description: A neoclassical grand dame on Piazza della Repubblica, old-Milan splendour on a generous scale.

items.name: Grand Hotel et de Milan
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: Milan's historic grand hotel since 1863, Verdi's home for decades, steps from La Scala.

items.name: Casa Cipriani Milano
items.description: A members'-club-style house of quiet exclusivity, the Cipriani sense of ease, brought to central Milan.

items.name: Palazzo Parigi Hotel & Grand Spa
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: A light-filled palazzo on the edge of Brera, marble, French windows and one of Milan's largest hotel spas.

items.name: Excelsior Hotel Gallia, a Luxury Collection Hotel
items.description: A 1932 Art Deco landmark by Centrale station, Milan's largest hotel spa and a celebrated rooftop over the city.

items.name: Bulgari, Château Monfort
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: A fairy-tale Art Nouveau castle near the Giardini, theatrical, romantic and a little out of the ordinary.

items.name: Vico Milano
items.description: A sleek, design-led newcomer in the towers of Porta Nuova, contemporary Milan at its most current.

items.name: Milano Verticale | UNA Esperienze
items.description: A sleek vertical hotel in the towers of Porta Nuova, contemporary Milan, with a Michelin-starred kitchen inside.

items.name: Senato Hotel Milano
items.description: A serene, all-white design boutique built around a courtyard, 43 rooms of quiet Milanese taste.

items.name: Rosa Grand Milano, Starhotels Collezione
items.description: A polished, well-run house a minute from the Duomo, location above all.

items.name: Room Mate Giulia
items.description: A design hotel tucked right beside the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, you cannot stay more central.

items.name: The Yard Milano
items.description: A quirky, sport-and-vintage-themed townhouse hotel with real personality, near Porta Romana.

items.name: Maison Borella
items.description: A restored canal-side house on the Naviglio Grande, a rare pocket of calm on the water.

items.name: Duomo di Milano (Milan Cathedral)
credentials: MICHELIN Green Guide ★★★, worth a special journey
One of the largest cathedrals in the world
items.description: The vast pink-Candoglia-marble Gothic cathedral that took nearly six centuries to build is the emotional centre of Milan and the natural first stop for a multi-generational family. Book a skip-the-line entry so grandparents move straight in from the piazza rather than queueing in the sun.

items.name: Duomo Rooftop Terraces
credentials: MICHELIN Green Guide ★★★, worth a special journey
items.description: You walk among 3,400 statues, spires and flying buttresses in Candoglia marble, with the Alps on the horizon on a clear day and the golden Madonnina overhead. Take the lift rather than the 251 steps for older relatives and small children, and go late afternoon for the light.

items.name: The Last Supper (Il Cenacolo), Santa Maria delle Grazie
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Church and Dominican Convent of Santa Maria delle Grazie with 'The Last Supper' by Leonardo da Vinci (inscribed 1980)
MICHELIN Green Guide ★★★, worth a special journey
items.description: Leonardo da Vinci's fragile 1490s mural survives on the refectory wall of a Dominican convent, seen by only small timed groups for 15 minutes at a time. Tickets vanish months ahead, so this is exactly the sort of unlock a concierge should secure well before you travel.

items.name: Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II
credentials: One of the world's oldest active shopping arcades (opened 1877)
items.description: The soaring 1877 glass-and-iron arcade linking the Duomo to La Scala is both a monument and the world's oldest luxury shopping mall, home to the original Prada boutique, Louis Vuitton, and the historic Camparino bar. Spin your heel on the mosaic bull for luck, then let the family browse in cool shade.

items.name: Teatro alla Scala (La Scala)
credentials: MICHELIN Green Guide ★★, worth a detour
One of the world's leading opera houses
items.description: Opened in 1778, La Scala is the most storied opera house on earth, where Verdi and Puccini premiered and where a box for the season opener is one of Milan's true social currencies. Pair a performance with the adjoining museum for the daytime members of a multi-gen group.

items.name: Quadrilatero della Moda (Fashion Quadrilateral)
credentials: Among the most expensive and prestigious luxury shopping districts in the world
items.description: The grid of Via Montenapoleone, Via della Spiga, Via Sant'Andrea and Via Manzoni is the densest concentration of maison flagships in the world, Armani, Prada, Versace, Dolce & Gabbana, Bottega, Hermes. Ask for private appointments and after-hours boutique openings; this is the reason many UHNI travellers come to Milan at all.

items.name: Castello Sforzesco (Sforza Castle)
credentials: MICHELIN Green Guide ★★, worth a detour
items.description: The vast 15th-century Sforza fortress holds a cluster of civic museums including Michelangelo's unfinished final work, the Rondanini Pietà. The scale and open courtyards make it easy for children and grandparents to wander at their own pace before Parco Sempione behind it.

items.name: Pinacoteca di Brera
credentials: MICHELIN Green Guide ★★★, worth a special journey
One of Italy's foremost art collections
items.description: Milan's greatest picture gallery, with Raphael's Marriage of the Virgin, Mantegna's foreshortened Dead Christ and Piero della Francesca's Montefeltro Altarpiece. Compact enough for one focused visit, and set inside the atmospheric artists' quarter for lunch afterwards.

items.name: Brera District
items.description: The cobbled bohemian quarter around the Pinacoteca, with its botanical garden, art shops, antiques and candlelit trattorias, is the most romantic part of central Milan to stroll after dark. Quiet, walkable and discreet, ideal for an evening away from the crowds.

items.name: Museo Poldi Pezzoli
credentials: MICHELIN Green Guide ★★, worth a detour
items.description: A perfectly preserved 19th-century aristocrat's house-museum steps from the fashion streets, its most famous piece Pollaiuolo's Portrait of a Young Woman. Intimate and rarely crowded, a refined pause between boutique appointments.

items.name: Museo Bagatti Valsecchi
items.description: The Bagatti Valsecchi brothers built a lavish neo-Renaissance home in the 1880s and filled it with genuine 15th- and 16th-century art and furniture, then lived in it. One of Europe's best-preserved historic house-museums, and a hidden gem in the middle of the Quadrilatero.

items.name: Museo del Novecento
items.description: Milan's museum of 20th-century Italian art sits inside the Palazzo dell'Arengario on Piazza del Duomo, its spiral ramp opening onto Futurist masterpieces and a fourth-floor window framing the cathedral. The rooftop restaurant Giacomo Arengario has cathedral views for lunch.

items.name: Gallerie d'Italia, Piazza Scala
items.description: Three interconnected palazzi facing La Scala hold a superb collection of 19th- and 20th-century Italian art, from Canova bas-reliefs to Boccioni. Beautifully restored, air-conditioned and calm, a civilised refuge in the very centre.

items.name: Fondazione Prada
items.description: Rem Koolhaas/OMA transformed a 1910s distillery into a striking contemporary art campus, complete with a gold-leaf-clad 'Haunted House' and Wes Anderson's jewel-box Bar Luce. A design pilgrimage that appeals to the younger generation as much as serious collectors.

items.name: Pirelli HangarBicocca
items.description: A colossal former industrial hangar showing ambitious contemporary art, anchored by Anselm Kiefer's permanent 'The Seven Heavenly Palaces', seven leaning concrete towers up to 19 metres tall. Free to enter and genuinely awe-inspiring for all ages.

items.name: Navigli Canals
items.description: The Naviglio Grande and Naviglio Pavese canals, part of a system Leonardo helped engineer, are now a lively waterside quarter of aperitivo bars, vintage shops and the monthly antiques market. Charming to walk by day; for UHNI travellers a private canal-side dinner or a quiet aperitivo away from the student crowd works best.

items.name: Porta Nuova & Bosco Verticale
credentials: Bosco Verticale, International Highrise Award winner (2014) and CTBUH Best Tall Building Worldwide (2015)
items.description: Milan's gleaming business district around Piazza Gae Aulenti is crowned by the Bosco Verticale, Stefano Boeri's award-winning 'vertical forest' towers dressed in thousands of trees. A striking counterpoint to old Milan and a favourite with design-minded younger travellers.

items.name: Cimitero Monumentale
items.description: This vast 19th-century cemetery is an open-air museum of Italian funerary sculpture, with extravagant Art Nouveau and Art Deco tombs of Milan's great industrial families. Solemn, uncrowded and photographically extraordinary, a quietly moving hidden gem.

items.name: Corso Como & 10 Corso Como
items.description: The pedestrian Corso Como is home to the legendary concept store 10 Corso Como, founded by Carla Sozzani, a pioneering blend of fashion, design, gallery, bookshop and courtyard café. A one-stop distillation of Milanese taste for the shopping-focused.

items.name: Triennale Milano
items.description: Italy's leading museum of design and architecture, set in the elegant Palazzo dell'Arte on the edge of Parco Sempione, with the permanent Italian Design Museum and a rooftop restaurant. Essential for anyone who cares about how Milan became the world's design capital.

items.name: Fuorisalone & Salone del Mobile (in season)
credentials: Salone del Mobile, the world's largest furniture and design fair
items.description: Each April the world's design elite descends on Milan for the Salone del Mobile furniture fair and the citywide Fuorisalone installations across Brera, Tortona and 5vie. In season it is the single best week to be in Milan, book everything, hotels included, far in advance.

items.name: Basilica di Sant'Ambrogio
credentials: MICHELIN Green Guide ★★, worth a detour
One of the most ancient churches in Milan (consecrated 379–386 AD)
items.description: One of the oldest churches in Milan, founded by the city's patron Saint Ambrose in the 4th century, its austere Romanesque form a world away from the Gothic Duomo. A serene, deeply historic stop with beautiful golden mosaics.

items.name: Basilica di San Lorenzo Maggiore & Colonne di San Lorenzo
items.description: An early-Christian basilica fronted by 16 Roman columns, the finest surviving ancient Roman ruin in Milan, with the exquisite Cappella di Sant'Aquilino and its 4th-century mosaics inside. The colonnade square is a lively evening gathering spot in the Ticinese.

items.name: Villa Necchi Campiglio
credentials: Managed by FAI, Fondo per l'Ambiente Italiano
items.description: A 1930s rationalist villa with pool and tennis court, restored by the FAI and used as a film set (I Am Love, House of Gucci), offering a rare glimpse into moneyed Milanese domestic life between the wars. Its garden café is a discreet, elegant lunch.

items.name: Pinacoteca Ambrosiana
credentials: MICHELIN Green Guide ★★, worth a detour
Holds Leonardo da Vinci's Codex Atlanticus
items.description: Founded by Cardinal Federico Borromeo in 1618, this gallery holds Caravaggio's Basket of Fruit, Raphael's cartoon for the School of Athens, and pages of Leonardo's Codex Atlanticus. A serious, uncrowded collection a short walk from the Duomo.

items.name: Museo Nazionale Scienza e Tecnologia Leonardo da Vinci
credentials: Italy's largest science and technology museum
items.description: Italy's largest science and technology museum, with galleries of machines built from Leonardo's drawings plus a real submarine and vintage aircraft. The most reliable crowd-pleaser in the city for children and teenagers.

items.name: Parco Sempione & Arco della Pace
items.description: Milan's grand central park unfurls behind the Sforza Castle to the Napoleonic Arch of Peace, with the Torre Branca observation tower for aerial views. Green, walkable space for grandparents and children between the museums.

items.name: QC Termemilano (Spa)
items.description: A refined day-spa set in a historic building beside a stretch of the old Spanish city walls, with pools, saunas and a tram-carriage relaxation room. A restorative half-day for the adults while the family shops or sightsees.

items.name: Chiesa di San Maurizio al Monastero Maggiore
items.description: Nicknamed the 'Sistine Chapel of Milan', this modest 16th-century church interior is entirely covered in luminous frescoes by Bernardino Luini and his school. Free, uncrowded and utterly unexpected, a true hidden gem near the Last Supper.

items.name: Corso Vittorio Emanuele II & San Babila
items.description: The pedestrian high street running from the Duomo to Piazza San Babila is Milan's mainstream shopping spine, Italian and international brands, department stores and cafes. Useful for the family's everyday buys while serious shopping happens in the Quadrilatero next door.

items.name: Excelsior Milano & La Rinascente (rooftop)
items.description: La Rinascente, Italy's landmark department store beside the Duomo, has a seventh-floor terrace of food counters and bars looking straight onto the cathedral spires. A convenient, glamorous perch for a break with unbeatable views.

items.name: Fondazione Nicola Trussardi & Palazzo Marino (Piazza della Scala)
items.description: The elegant Piazza della Scala, anchored by the 16th-century Palazzo Marino (Milan's city hall) and a Leonardo monument, is one of the city's most photogenic squares. A graceful pause between La Scala and the shopping streets.

items.name: Chiostri dell'Umanitaria & Rotonda della Besana
items.description: The Rotonda della Besana is a serene 18th-century circular arcaded courtyard, once a cemetery, now a tranquil green enclosure with a baroque chapel. A calm, little-known spot for a quiet stroll away from any crowd.

items.name: Isola Neighbourhood
items.description: Once a working-class 'island' cut off by the railway, Isola is now Milan's coolest quarter, independent boutiques, natural-wine bars and design studios in the shadow of the Bosco Verticale. Best explored on foot for a feel of contemporary Milanese life.

items.name: Porta Venezia & Corso Venezia palazzi
items.description: Corso Venezia is lined with grand Liberty-style (Italian Art Nouveau) palaces and leads to the leafy Giardini Pubblici Indro Montanelli. An elegant residential quarter with fine dining and the city's Natural History Museum for children.

items.name: Aperitivo in Milan
items.description: The pre-dinner ritual of a Negroni or Milano-Torino with generous snacks was effectively invented here, Campari was born in Milan. For UHNI travellers, a reserved table at a rooftop bar such as Terrazza Aperol or a hotel bar beats the crowded street scene.

items.name: Historic Cafes: Camparino & Cova
credentials: Cova, one of Milan's oldest pastry shops (founded 1817)
items.description: Camparino in Galleria (1915) is the birthplace of the Campari ritual, while Pasticceria Cova on Via Montenapoleone has served Milanese society since 1817. Both are elegant, vegetarian-friendly stops for coffee, pastries and people-watching.

items.name: Lake Como (Bellagio, Como, Varenna)
credentials: MICHELIN Green Guide ★★★, worth a special journey
Villa del Balbianello and Villa Carlotta are among Italy's most celebrated lake villas
items.description: Under an hour by train or car, Lake Como delivers the classic Italian lakes fantasy, Bellagio's terraced gardens, Villa del Balbianello, Villa Carlotta and George Clooney's Laglio. Arrange a private boat and a villa lunch; this is the single most requested escape from Milan.

items.name: Bergamo Alta (Upper Town)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venetian Walls of Bergamo (part of 'Venetian Works of Defence between the 16th and 17th Centuries', inscribed 2017)
items.description: Less than an hour away, Bergamo's walled Città Alta is a beautifully intact medieval-Renaissance hill town reached by an 1887 funicular, crowned by the Piazza Vecchia and the Colleoni Chapel. Its Venetian walls are UNESCO-listed and its restaurants excellent and unhurried.

items.name: Lake Maggiore & the Borromean Islands
credentials: MICHELIN Green Guide ★★★, worth a special journey
Isola Bella, Palazzo Borromeo and its baroque garden
items.description: Around 90 minutes away, Lake Maggiore's Borromean Islands hold the baroque Palazzo Borromeo on Isola Bella, its terraced gardens roamed by white peacocks, and the fishing village of Isola dei Pescatori. Grander and quieter than Como, ideal for a private-boat day.

items.name: Certosa di Pavia
credentials: MICHELIN Green Guide ★★★, worth a special journey
One of the largest monasteries in Italy
items.description: Less than an hour south, this Carthusian charterhouse commissioned in 1396 by the Visconti dukes is one of the great masterpieces of Italian Gothic-Renaissance architecture, its facade a riot of marble sculpture. Serene, still a working monastery, and beautifully off the mainstream tourist trail.

items.name: Franciacorta Wine Country
credentials: Franciacorta DOCG, Italy's premier traditional-method sparkling wine region
items.description: About an hour east toward Lake Iseo, Franciacorta is Italy's answer to Champagne, rolling vineyards producing traditional-method sparkling wine, with elegant cellars offering private tastings and lunches. A refined, adult day out for oenophiles.

items.name: Pavia (Old University Town)
credentials: Home to the University of Pavia (founded 1361)
items.description: The medieval city on the Ticino river has one of Europe's oldest universities (1361), a distinctive covered bridge and towered skyline. Easily paired with the Certosa for a full, unhurried day away from Milan's bustle.

items.name: Enrico Bartolini al MUDEC
items.description: Milan's only three-star, Italy's most-decorated chef, on the top floor of the MUDEC museum.

items.name: Seta by Antonio Guida
items.description: Antonio Guida's two-star room at the Mandarin Oriental, Mediterranean precision, faultlessly served.

items.name: Andrea Aprea
items.area: Porta Venezia (Fondazione Luigi Rovati, Corso Venezia)
items.description: Aprea's elegant two-star atop the Rovati foundation, contemporary Italian with a Neapolitan soul.

items.name: Il Luogo di Aimo e Nadia
items.description: A Milanese institution, Negrini and Pisani carrying forward one of Italy's great kitchens.

items.name: Verso
items.description: The Capitaneo brothers' assured two-star, refined, personal cooking near the Duomo.

items.name: Cracco in Galleria
items.description: Carlo Cracco's grand dining room inside the Galleria itself, the most glamorous address in Milan.

items.name: IYO Aalto
items.description: Takeshi Iwai's ambitious Japanese-European tasting room in the Porta Nuova towers.

items.name: Langosteria
items.description: Milan's glamorous seafood temple, oysters, crustaceans and the catch of the day, done with real flair.

items.name: Contraste
items.description: Matias Perdomo's playful, boundary-pushing tasting menu in an intimate townhouse room.

items.name: Berton
items.description: Andrea Berton's clean, modern cooking in the glass towers of Porta Nuova, broths and clarity are his signature.

items.name: Sadler
items.description: Claudio Sadler's long-held star, classical technique and Milanese elegance, quietly enduring.

items.name: Viva Viviana Varese
items.description: Viviana Varese's bold, sustainability-minded cooking, one of the city's most personal kitchens.

items.name: IYO
items.description: Italy's first starred Japanese restaurant, the room that proved sushi could be haute in Milan.

items.name: Horto
items.description: Norbert Niederkofler's radically seasonal 'Cook the Mountain' ethos, on a rooftop above the centre.

items.name: Joia
items.description: Europe's first vegetarian restaurant to win a star, Pietro Leemann's meditative, plant-led cooking.

items.name: L'Alchimia
items.description: A polished modern-Milanese room with a cocktail-bar heart, refined cooking, easy warmth.

items.name: Anima
items.description: A confident hotel-restaurant star in Porta Nuova, contemporary Italian with technical polish.

items.name: Sine by Di Pinto
items.description: Roberto Di Pinto's personal, southern-rooted cooking, one of the city's warmest starred rooms.

items.name: Procaccini
items.description: A newly-starred room of very personal cooking and live piano each evening, raw material, technique, hospitality.

items.name: Abba
items.description: Fabio Abbattista's 2024 debut, starred within a year, precise, well-travelled contemporary cooking.

items.name: Ratanà
items.description: Cesare Battisti's love letter to Lombard cooking, the yellow risotto alla milanese, done properly.

items.name: Trattoria Trippa
items.description: Diego Rossi's cult trattoria, offal, Milanese classics and Italian regional cooking, done with real conviction.

items.name: Dongiò
items.description: A beloved family-run Calabrian trattoria, 'nduja, fresh pasta and southern warmth, unchanged for decades.

items.name: L'Angolo d'Abruzzo
items.description: Generous, homely Abruzzese cooking in enormous portions, a great-value Milan institution.

items.name: Serendib
items.description: Milan's long-loved Sri Lankan and Indian table, the name means 'happy land', and it delivers.

items.name: La Cucina dei Frigoriferi Milanesi
items.description: Modern Italian cooking in the revived Palazzo del Ghiaccio complex, creative and good value.

items.name: Le Nove Scodelle
items.description: Serious, fiery Sichuan cooking, a reminder that some of Milan's best value is well beyond the centre.

items.name: Confine
credentials: 50 Top Pizza Italy 2025, No. 2 in Italy
items.description: The best pizza in Milan, Neapolitan rounds, fried, padellino and gourmet slices, with a wine list to match.

items.name: Dry Milano
credentials: 50 Top Pizza Italy 2025, No. 7 in Italy
items.description: The pizza-and-cocktails original that redefined the Milanese evening, great pies, better drinks.

items.name: Marghe
items.description: Honest, well-made Neapolitan pizza across the city, a dependable, everyday favourite.

items.name: Pasticceria Marchesi 1824
items.description: Milan's most elegant historic pasticceria, a Prada-owned jewel-box for coffee and pastries under the Galleria.

items.name: Pavé
items.description: A modern Milanese bakery beloved for its brioche and pastries, the city's best morning ritual.

items.name: Camparino in Galleria
items.description: The birthplace of the Milanese aperitivo, a Liberty-style bar under the Galleria, where Campari itself was born.

items.name: Bar Basso
credentials: Where the Negroni Sbagliato was invented (1972)
items.description: The birthplace of the Negroni Sbagliato, an unchanging 1960s institution and the temple of Milanese aperitivo.

items.name: Moebius Milano
credentials: World's 50 Best Bars, best in Italy on the list
items.description: Milan's highest-ranked bar, a food-music-and-cocktails concept of rare coherence, and the world's Highest Climber of its year.
A password-and-membership speakeasy of quiet excellence, one of Italy's most consistently ranked bars.

items.name: Nottingham Forest
items.description: A tiny, cult tiki-and-molecular bar that has long featured among the world's best, theatre in a glass.

items.name: Terrazza Aperol
credentials: A landmark aperitivo terrace overlooking the Duomo
items.description: An aperitivo terrace looking straight onto the Duomo, the most Milanese spritz there is.

items.name: Ceresio 7
credentials: A landmark rooftop bar atop a Dsquared2-designed building
items.description: Dsquared2's rooftop bar and pools above the old Enel building, glamour, a spritz and a sweep over the skyline.

items.name: Dry Milano
items.description: The pizza-and-cocktails original, a Brera room where the drinks are as serious as the pies.

plan.heading: 3 days in Milan, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

days.label: Day 1
days.title: The Duomo and the Last Supper

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Arrive at the Mandarin Oriental, then the Duomo and its rooftop terraces.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Leonardo's Last Supper by timed reservation at Santa Maria delle Grazie.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Seta at the Mandarin Oriental, two Michelin stars.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The Pinacoteca di Brera for the Mantegna and the Piero della Francesca.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The Montenapoleone quarter and the maison flagships, then aperitivo in Brera.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Enrico Bartolini at the Mudec, three Michelin stars.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The Fondazione Prada or the Museo Poldi Pezzoli, an intimate collection.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A car to Lake Como, the villas at Cernobbio, an afternoon at Villa d'Este.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner lakeside at Villa d'Este before returning, or an early train home.

items.name: Brera
items.description: Cobbled artists' quarter with galleries and the best strolling, the romantic base.

items.name: Quadrilatero della Moda
items.description: The luxury shopping grid around Montenapoleone, for the serious shopper.

items.name: Navigli
items.description: Canalside bars and aperitivo, for a livelier, younger evening scene.

events.name: Milan Fashion Week
events.note: The women's shows twice a year turn the city into fashion's world capital.

events.name: Salone del Mobile (Design Week)
events.note: The world's biggest furniture and design fair, spilling into installations across every district.

events.name: Sant'Ambrogio & La Scala opening night
events.note: The city's patron-saint feast and the opera season's gala premiere on the same night.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Stay in the Quadrilatero della Moda or Brera for the best of the city; Milan dresses sharply, so an elegant wardrobe is expected, and Como, the lakes and the Alps are an easy day's drive with a car.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Fly into Malpensa or the closer Linate; a chauffeured car handles the transfer, with Linate only about 15 minutes from the centre.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A private driver for the city and the lakes, while the fashion quarter and centre around the Duomo are best walked.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Strong everywhere; a TIM or Vodafone eSIM works well, with fast wifi in hotels.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Euro; cards are accepted throughout and cash is rarely needed; service is generally included, so tipping is minimal.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: May-June and September-October are best: mild, clear and comfortable for the city and lakes. Avoid humid, hazy July-August and the cold, fog-prone damp of December-January.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: Air India flies nonstop Delhi-Milan Malpensa, about 9.5 hours on a Boeing 787 Dreamliner, roughly four times weekly; Mumbai and Bengaluru connect neatly via a Gulf hub. Malpensa is calmer than Fiumicino; pre-arrange a car for the 50-minute run into the city or on to Lake Como.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No vaccinations beyond routine; safe, with ordinary care against pickpocketing around the Duomo, Centrale station and on the metro. Tap water is safe to drink.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Vegetarian dining is straightforward; Jain and strict no-onion-garlic want advance notice. A fair Indian presence exists, but Milan's strength is refined vegetarian Italian; the advisor should brief fine-dining kitchens, which accommodate readily.
